name: Glimmerwing
lore: Its wings sense disturbances in the field and pull its light body toward the source. Near old relays, glimmerwings were mistaken for sparks from damaged wiring.

name: Furrow Leech
lore: Soft segments let it squeeze beneath node foundations. Its tracks appear inside sealed housings. Crews learned to check the floor before opening a cover.

name: Glass Adder
lore: Its body disappears among cracks in the shallows. Young adders gather around warm supports. Adults enter the Hollow Contour and return with darkened joints.

name: Longstride
lore: It places its feet in the same hollows between slabs. Generations share one path. When a Core crosses it, the measured gait changes.

name: Flow Hound
lore: Observers thought the animal had been tamed: it faithfully followed a moving node. It stopped waiting only after the node halted and grew cold.

name: Relay Moth
lore: Dust on its wings gathers the light of standby lamps. Moths settle along cable runs in empty stations. When power returns, the entire ceiling moves.

name: Clicker
lore: Two hard plates lie beneath its shell. Their tapping comes before its legs emerge from a crack. In empty passages, the sound answers itself.

name: Pier Beetle
lore: Its shell grows in layers, gathering mineral dust around Network foundations. Old beetles carry rusted fasteners on their backs. The metal cannot be shaken loose.

name: Slab Breaker
lore: It lives beneath fallen ceilings. Fresh rubble pushed outside betrays its presence. Workers trusted a collapse only after it remained unchanged for a week.

name: Linkbreaker
lore: Its tracks appeared between intact nodes. Neither was damaged, yet the Network would no longer close across the gap.

name: Rhythm Eater
lore: The pack moves more quietly around it. The field drains gradually. Observers noticed only when a relay went dark.

name: Phantom Hunter
lore: The hunter remembers where it lost its prey. Each return finds a shorter route to that place.

name: Pattern Shifter
lore: Plans around its mark are heavily corrected. Each distance is accurate. No crew could fit them into one drawing.

name: Elder Brood
lore: More than one rhythm sounds beneath its old shell. Its tracks look as though a tightly packed group passed there.

name: Mirror Warden
lore: Its armor bears no deep scars. The things that should have made them were found in walls behind the attacker.

name: Stasis Warden
lore: Dust settles slowly beside the warden. A surviving camera recorded motionless grains with swift shadows around them.

name: Nullifier
lore: The lamps behind it are intact. They light up after it leaves, as though someone finally releases a switch.

name: Ash Carrier
lore: Its trail stays warm even on cold glass. A dry crackle sounds within the shell. The seams never quite close.

name: Elder Gatherer
lore: It lives beside empty stores and checks every corner, as though remembering exactly what used to lie there.

name: Void Lancer
lore: Scouts marked it with a narrow puncture on their maps. Distance did not help: the mark appeared where the observer had just stood.

name: Breacher
lore: A basin crossing bears its name. It commemorates no victory. The former passage vanished when the creature first reached the surface.

name: Brood Mind
lore: It was mistaken for a gathering place for smaller creatures. An empty shell revealed that the swarm shared one very old body.

name: Aura Titan
lore: It passes the nodes without touching them. Broken links and a few seconds of absolute silence remain behind.

name: Stranger Conductor
lore: The recording contains one measure. Every instrument then adopted a shared rhythm present in none of their settings.

name: Blind Architect
lore: It completes outlines around an empty center. Missing sections are restored precisely. Every passage the builders left open is closed.

name: The Null
lore: There is a timestamp before it appears and another afterward. Between them lies neither image nor recording fault. Only a difference in the number who returned.

name: Stella Warden
lore: The warden never strays far from the stabilization node. Its orders contain no command to attack. One line survives: do not allow operation to cease.

name: Stillwater Monitor
lore: It has no cruising engine. In peacetime it was towed into orbit. It never left its final station.

name: Mine Sloop
lore: Signs beside the hatches forbid ignition near munitions. Every sign is scorched on one side.

name: Screen Corvette
lore: Tow-clamp scars remain on its armor. It pulled damaged vessels out of formation. It now fills the gaps itself.

name: Jamming Vessel
lore: Its antennas point into the formation. The order to suppress foreign signals was the last to name an enemy.

name: Choir Command Node
lore: Fourteen command voices remain. They speak together whenever an order is sent. The ships still understand.

name: Seam Picket
lore: The picket remained between two fading lines of lights. Its command module still requests permission to change station.

name: Patch Repair Ship
lore: Its arms cannot distinguish old damage from new. It keeps returning to holes left in the final battle.

name: Drain Collector
lore: It followed the fleet collecting spent cells. Its holds are full. The collection route remains unfinished.

name: Far Side Scout
lore: It tested the passage first. Its arrival record predates its departure by eleven minutes.

name: Ligature Gunship
lore: Logs marked these gunships with a stroke. The gunner added a second after returning. The final log contains no second strokes.

name: Stray Hull Tug
lore: Rings from different yards hang from its clamps. It found ships by distress beacons and seldom waited for an answer.

name: Fine Edge Frigate
lore: Built to fire through shield gaps, its targeting drives outlived yard and crew without losing calibration.

name: Needle Interceptor
lore: There is no room for a spare reactor. Pilots exchanged craft after every sortie. The final exchange never took place.

name: Threshold Ironclad
lore: Plates from three ships reinforce its flank. One retains a watch schedule on the inside. No one remains to read it.

name: Far Shore Carrier
lore: The carrier retains a landing register but no departure list. Drones leave with clean callsigns. Those it accepts back are already familiar.

name: Tunnel Plug
lore: It grew around a passage. Moving scrapes masonry from its shell. The passage remains closed.

name: Burst Sac
lore: Its hatching chamber stands apart. There is no permanent entrance. After each cycle, the insects cut a new one.

name: Gate Ram
lore: Generations were bred beside the sealed gates. The gates fell. Every member of the brood still carries the broad forehead.

name: Mold Carrier
lore: The growth first appeared on sealed medical crates. They opened from within, and the first carrier crossed the corridor.

name: Hush Drone
lore: It is noticed by the missing rustle. In the hive's quiet chamber, even footsteps seem absent beside it.

name: Casemate Worker
lore: The broods cleared the stairs. Steps grew wider and walls thinner. The bastion's builders could no longer use these passages.

name: Resin Nurse
lore: Resin comes from the hive roots. The nurse carries it between patrols. Old soldiers know its scent in darkness.

name: Cistern Leech
lore: The cisterns dried out long ago. Their leeches remained beside the pipes and learned to find other warm currents.

name: Crack Walker
lore: At night, patrols heard scraping inside the walls. The masonry stayed intact, with footprints appearing outside.

name: Spore Spitter
lore: Its throat sacs hold dust from the lower chambers. It hangs in the empty bastion. Marks on the walls betrayed its passing.

name: Clutch Bearer
lore: Young cling to folds beneath its abdomen. Even in an abandoned corridor, the bearer is never alone.

name: Brood Runner
lore: Creases from its hatching membrane remain on the shell. It does not know the passages and follows the older brood.

name: Hive Shieldbearer
lore: A young shell lies beneath the dark plates. Shieldbearers inherit both old armor and a place in the patrol.

name: Brood Queen
lore: The queen settled in the command casemate, where walls held warmth longest. Broods changed and passages closed. Her tracks at the entrance remained the same.

name: Keystone Monolith
lore: It hangs above a collapsed support. Its underside retains the imprint of a beam lost years ago.

name: Strained Geode
lore: The geode looks whole outside. Inside, each reflection is displaced from the next. Watching it for long is uncomfortable.

name: Clouded Crystal
lore: A gray vein reaches the surface at its joints. Similar veins appeared in neighboring samples after transport.

name: Fault Tuning Fork
lore: Its prongs vibrate at slightly different rates. Instruments between them give accurate readings that change every time.

name: Chipling
lore: It stays beside its parent rock. The hollow left in the wall is too smooth to be a natural fracture.

name: Facet Mender
lore: Thin filaments reach neighboring crystals. After a collapse, they reform before the dust settles.

name: Hollow Facet
lore: The specimen outweighed its carrier vessel. At the next stop, the vessel was full and the specimen gone.

name: Facet Shooter
lore: The front crack resembles a tool mark. Even young specimens that have never seen a drilling rig bear it.

name: Needle Lens
lore: Its central facet shows a distant wall through opaque rock. The first lens was lost with its observer.

name: Cluster Guard
lore: Old drill tips are visible inside the cluster. The crystal closed around them and kept growing.

name: Thunder Blister
lore: Blisters grow where opposing currents meet. Surviving paths curve widely around these places.

name: Thunder Wedge
lore: Branching burns remain on the supports. Every mark points toward the long-extinguished beacon.

name: Fouled Discharge
lore: The arc leaves a black deposit on metal. Traces beneath it are intact but no longer conduct.

name: Beat Breaker
lore: One watch clock lost seven seconds during a shift. The clock beside it gained seven.

name: Wandering Pulse
lore: It returns to its birthplace after every circuit. No transmitter remains, but the pause before departure is always the same.

name: Current Mender
lore: It pauses beside severed conductors. Light bridges them, though the old circuit has no power source.

name: Return Current
lore: Switched-off instruments wake for a fraction of a second. Their capacitors are completely empty afterward.

name: Interval
lore: It appears between bright flashes. The surface where its trail should be remains cold.

name: Arc Shooter
lore: The arc traces an old antenna's outline. Even its broken stays become visible during discharge.

name: Straight Lightning
lore: Its trail never branches. The first photographs were judged damaged: one straight line crossed several frames.

name: Spark Swarm
lore: Instruments treated it as interference. Then the sparks began moving around obstacles and waiting for one another.

name: Fixed Address
lore: The vault was relocated many times. Its index retains an old coordinate. Something still occupies that position.

name: Emergency Dump
lore: The protocol required destruction after overflow. The counter was reset. The command remains queued.

name: Damaged Cast
lore: Traces of incompatible bodies cover it. Sometimes one movement ends before the next begins.

name: Redactor
lore: It does not destroy a record. It removes a short passage after which the rest no longer makes sense.

name: Body Draft
lore: The record has no completion date. The archive retrieves it from temporary storage and marks it unfinished once more.

name: Restorer
lore: It closes gaps without the original. Foreign fragments take hold so firmly that the archive loses their boundaries.

name: Name Collector
lore: Blank lines appear in the visitor log. Arrival times are correct. The name fields look untouched.

name: Omission
lore: A space separates consecutive inventory numbers. It cannot be removed. After verification, the gap returns.

name: Lost Fragment Gatherer
lore: It brings scraps of voices and body parts to a closed door. The door never opens. The pile grows.

name: Last Witness
lore: The recording ends with one precise shot. On each replay, the shooter finds the position from which it was watched.

name: Backup Copy
lore: The record saved itself in several locations. Each version considers the others restoration errors.

name: Runaway Copy
lore: It separated before verification ended. Its route contains turns absent from every surviving map.

name: Shell Keeper
lore: The protective layers do not match. Each covers a crack in the previous one and clings to it.

name: Spherist
lore: He built his first Network from nodes with incompatible sockets. The workshop considered it temporary. By the time replacements arrived, the Network answered only to him. He still carries an adapter with nothing left to connect.

name: Hunter
lore: The Hunter returned without a map. Scratches covered the Core: distances, pauses, directions. Asked to reconstruct his route, he reconstructed the positions of those following him.

name: Engineer
lore: His first post was keeper of the reserve line. It went unused for seven years. On the day of the accident, it became the station's only working system. The Engineer dislikes hearing a spare node called unnecessary.

name: Berserker
lore: A dent remains in the Core's armor. A replacement casing has long been ready. The Berserker postpones the work. Through the old metal, he can hear how close the pack has come.

name: Alchemist
lore: She labels vessels with times rather than contents. The same mixture behaves differently an hour later, and differently again the next day. Her journal contains more crossed-out dates than formulas.

name: Architect
lore: The Architect draws the Network before placing its first node. A space remains at the edge. A partner's Sphere once stood there. He has not learned to redraw the plan completely.

name: Conductor
lore: After communications failed, he maintained the rhythm by hand for days. Clocks stopped; the nodes kept answering. He returned, but still counts pauses as though no transmitter were nearby.

name: Oracle
lore: The Oracle never answers immediately. First she moves an object no one has intended to touch. Her room holds few belongings. The walls bear marks from former shelves.

name: Voidwalker
lore: The transit log records his name twice in one minute, at opposite ends of the route. Both signatures are authentic. He wants to know only who wrote the second.

name: Fractal
lore: He keeps several versions of one design. Each corrects a different mistake; none is finished. Before leaving, he lays them side by side. Another sheet sometimes appears on his return.
